on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - 'src/**'
      - 'test/**'
      - 'package.json'
jobs:
  Ubuntu:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20.x
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: 8
      
      - name: Install Backend-Server
        run: pnpm install

      - name: Build Swagger
        run: npm run build:swagger

      - name: Build SDK
        run: npm run build:sdk

      - name: Compile Backend-Server
        run: npm run build

      - name: Run Test Program
        run: npm run test -- --simultaneous 16

      - name: EsLint
        run: npm run eslint

# AutoBE Generated Backend Server

![AutoBE Logo](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a90d14be-fd50-4dc7-ae9d-ca66c2124f31)

A backend repository generated by [`@autobe`](https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe).

This backend program was automatically generated using [`@autobe`](https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe), the AI vibe coding agent for backend servers of below stack.

- TypeScript
- NestJS / Nestia
- Prisma
- Postgres

## Project Structure

This template project has categorized directories like below.

As you can see from the below, all of the Backend source files are placed into the [src](src/) directory. When you build the TypeScript source files, compiled files would be placed into the `lib` directory following the [tsconfig.json](tsconfig.json) configuration. Otherwise you build client [SDK](#32-sdk) library for npm publishing and their compiled files would be placed into the [packages](packages) directory.

  - [packages/api/](packages/api): SDK module built by `npm run build:api`
  - [src/](src): Backend source directory
    - [src/api/](src/api/): Client SDK that would be published to the `@ORGANIZATION/PROJECT-api`
      - [**src/api/functional/**](src/api/functional/): API functions generated by the [`nestia`](https://github.com/samchon/nestia)
      - [**src/api/structures/**](src/api/structures/): DTO structures
    - [src/controllers/](src/controllers/): Controller classes of the Main Program
  - [**test/**](test): Test Automation Program
    - [test/features](test/features): List of test functions
  - [nestia.config.ts](nestia.config.ts): Configuration file of [`nestia`](https://github.com/samchon/nestia)
  - [package.json](package.json): NPM configuration
  - [tsconfig.json](tsconfig.json): TypeScript configuration for the main program

## NPM Run Commands

List of the run commands defined in the [package.json](package.json) are like below:

  - Test
    - **`test`**: Run test automation program
    - `benchmark`: Run performance benchmark program
  - Build
    - `build`: Build everything
    - `build:main`: Build main program (`src` directory)
    - `build:test` Build test automation program (`test` directory)
    - `build:sdk`: Build SDK into main program only
    - `build:swagger`: Build Swagger Documents
    - **`dev`**: Incremental build for development (test program)
  - Deploy
    - `package:api`: Build and deploy the SDK library to the NPM
    - `start`: Start the backend server
    - `start:dev`: Start the backend server with incremental build and reload
  - Webpack
    - `webpack`: Run webpack bundler
    - `webpack:start`: Start the backend server built by webpack
    - `webpack:test`: Run test program to the webpack built

## Specialization

Transform this template project to be yours.

When you've created a new backend project through this template project, you can specialize it to be suitable for you by changing some words. Replace below words through IDE specific function like `Edit > Replace in Files` (*Ctrl + Shift + H*), who've been supported by the VSCode.

| Before       | After
|--------------|----------------------------------------
| ORGANIZATION | Your account or corporation name
| PROJECT      | Your own project name
| AUTHOR       | Author name
| https://github.com/samchon/nestia-start | Your repository URL

# SDK Library
This is a SDK library generated by [`nestia`](https://nestia.io).

With this SDK library, you can easily and safely interact with backend server.

Just import and call some API functions like gif image below:

![nestia-sdk-demo](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/13158709/215004990-368c589d-7101-404e-b81b-fbc936382f05.gif)

> Left is server code, and right is client code utilizing the SDK




# What [`Nestia`](https://nestia.io) is:
![Nestia Logo](https://nestia.io/logo.png)

[![GitHub license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](https://github.com/samchon/nestia/blob/master/LICENSE)
[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@nestia/core.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nestia/core)
[![Downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/@nestia/core.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nestia/core)
[![Build Status](https://github.com/samchon/nestia/workflows/build/badge.svg)](https://github.com/samchon/nestia/actions?query=workflow%3Abuild)
[![Guide Documents](https://img.shields.io/badge/guide-documents-forestgreen)](https://nestia.io/docs/)

Nestia is a set of helper libraries for NestJS, supporting below features:

  - `@nestia/core`: super-fast decorators
  - `@nestia/sdk`:
    - Swagger generator evolved than ever
    - SDK library generator for clients
    - Mockup Simulator for client applications
    - Automatic E2E test functions generator
  - `@nestia/migrate`: migration from Swagger to NestJS
  - `nestia`: just CLI (command line interface) tool

> **Note**
> 
> - **Only one line** required, with pure TypeScript type
> - Enhance performance **30x** up
>   - Runtime validator is **20,000x faster** than `class-validator`
>   - JSON serialization is **200x faster** than `class-transformer`
> - Software Development Kit
>   - SDK is a collection of `fetch` functions with type definitions like [tRPC](https://trpc.io/)
>   - Mockup simulator means embedded backend simulator in SDK
>     - similar with [msw](https://mswjs.io/), but fully automated

import { Controller } from "@nestjs/common";
import { TypedRoute, TypedBody, TypedParam } from "@nestia/core";
import typia, { tags } from "typia";

import { IUser } from "../../../api/structures/IUser";
import { IPageIUser } from "../../../api/structures/IPageIUser";

@Controller("/core/users")
export class CoreUsersController {
  /**
   * Create a new user in the Core users table.
   *
   * This API enables the creation of a new user as defined in the 'users'
   * table of the Core Prisma DB schema. The required input includes core user
   * profile values such as username, email, role assignment, organization,
   * and password (hashed by business logic before storage). The onboarding
   * process enforces unique constraints for username and email, validates
   * organizational and role alignment, and securely stores credentials by
   * hashing passwords before database insertion.
   *
   * Operations are permission-gated—only administrators or automated systems
   * with proper authentication can invoke this endpoint. Each create action
   * is logged for compliance and future evidence audits, capturing both the
   * actor and the precise input (excluding the raw password). Upon success,
   * the complete, newly created user record is returned, suitable for
   * downstream integrations or immediate administrative review.
   *
   * Business logic covers duplicate key detection (username/email), correct
   * organizational/role association, and required data field validation.
   * Error responses cover all input, permission, and system error classes,
   * with well-defined codes for each.
   *
   * Related endpoints include listing, reading, updating, and deleting user
   * accounts. Used in onboarding, administrative user management, and
   * automated provisioning workflows.
   *
   * @param body Core user creation payload (username, email, password, org,
   *   role, etc.)
   * @autobe Generated by AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
   */
  @TypedRoute.Post()
  public async post(
    @TypedBody()
    body: IUser.ICreate,
  ): Promise<IUser> {
    body;
    return typia.random<IUser>();
  }

  /**
   * Retrieve a paginated, filterable list of users from the Core users table.
   *
   * This API provides an extensive list operation for users, referencing the
   * 'users' table in the Core schema as described in the Prisma schema
   * comments. The endpoint is designed to support comprehensive search and
   * filtering using various user properties, such as username, email,
   * organization ID, and role ID.
   *
   * Security is paramount—only authorized personnel (e.g., admins or managers
   * with the proper permissions) can utilize this endpoint. Every query
   * operation is logged for audit and evidence preservation, supporting full
   * traceability for compliance. The returned user list includes detailed
   * user attributes but redacts sensitive values like password hashes.
   * Pagination and sorting parameters enable efficient navigation of large
   * datasets while maintaining strict performance SLAs.
   *
   * The operation implements business logic checks for soft-deleted users,
   * filtered by the deleted_at field as required by regulatory and audit
   * standards. Error handling covers validation of query parameters,
   * permission denials, and system-level failures, delivering appropriate
   * feedback for each scenario.
   *
   * Related API operations include user creation, single-user detail
   * retrieval, updates, and deletions. This endpoint is commonly paired with
   * auditing and access log endpoints to deliver a complete administrative
   * user management suite.
   *
   * @param body Search, filter, and pagination options for user retrieval.
   * @autobe Generated by AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
   */
  @TypedRoute.Patch()
  public async patch(
    @TypedBody()
    body: IUser.IRequest,
  ): Promise<IPageIUser> {
    body;
    return typia.random<IPageIUser>();
  }

  /**
   * Fetch detailed user record by ID from the Core users table.
   *
   * This endpoint fetches detailed information about a specific user,
   * referencing the 'users' table in the Core Prisma DB schema. The returned
   * profile includes attributes like username, email, organizational and role
   * assignments, creation and update timestamps, and account status, while
   * excluding sensitive hash fields for security reasons.
   *
   * The operation enforces strict authentication and role-based permission
   * logic, ensuring that only authorized entities—such as administrators or
   * the user themselves—can access personal data. Access to deleted or
   * inactive users is restricted; queries to such entities result in clear
   * error messages for evidence and compliance.
   *
   * All access to user details is audited, preserving a tamper-evident log
   * for regulatory and forensic analysis. Error scenarios include not found,
   * unauthorized access, and internal server errors, with structured
   * responses for each.
   *
   * Typically used in conjunction with operations listing users, creating new
   * accounts, and updating or deleting records. This endpoint is essential
   * for administrative dashboards, compliance reviews, and user-facing
   * profile screens.
   *
   * @param id User ID (UUID) of the target user.
   * @autobe Generated by AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe

  }

  /**
   * Update an existing user record by ID in the Core users table.
   *
   * This operation updates an existing user identified by their unique ID,
   * referencing the 'users' table in the Core Prisma DB schema. Supported
   * updates include username, email, phone, role, organization assignment,
   * is_active status, etc., except for immutable fields like the user ID and
   * password hash (which is only updated through secure password reset

   *
   * Authorization is enforced by role-based rules—only privileged users or
   * system processes may update other user records, with self-update controls

   * Validation checks enforce uniqueness (for username, email), correct
